why: The revamped grok-run rejects contracts before launch. It cost three relaunch attempts because a contract can read as rigorous to a human and still parse as EMPTY to the gate.

what_the_gate_actually_parses.commands: ONLY from BACKTICK-quoted strings containing cargo|npm|pytest|go|make|node|pnpm|yarn. An indented code block is INVISIBLE to it.
what_the_gate_actually_parses.write_roots: from lines led by EDIT / WRITE / OUTPUT, or containing modify|edit|change|implement|write|create|add|fix|refactor|touch - with the path on the SAME line. A prose list of paths under a '## WRITE SCOPE' heading is invisible.
what_the_gate_actually_parses.verification_roots: lines led by VERIFY, or containing verify|test|tests must|run the tests
what_the_gate_actually_parses.acceptance: the word acceptance, or 'must pass', or 'exit 0'

the_four_errors_it_raises: NO_ACCEPTANCE - nothing can mark the task done
NO_VERIFICATION - no test path and no runnable command
UNBOUNDED_WRITE - asks for changes but names no writable path
CONTRADICTORY_PATHS - a path is both writable and denied
working_template: Use '## VERIFY' with a backticked `cargo ...` command, and one '## EDIT <path>' line per writable root, plus 'DENY <path>' lines for files concurrent lanes own.
my_assessment: The gate is right and I was wrong to find it obstructive. Every rejection named a real hole: my catalog contract had no machine-checkable command and no bounded write scope, which is exactly how two lanes collided on qwen38_hybrid_decode.rs earlier today and forced a manual conflict resolution. Do not reach for SG_OFF - fix the contract.
